human_review_reasons: Inference and generation-time evidence cannot be tied to an exact hardware environment, and the claimed mobile benefit remains an unmeasured expectation.
The normalized source omits referenced table-cell values, preventing reconciliation of exact per-variant VBench, FLOP, and generation-time comparisons.

assumptions: Efficient attention inside a video diffusion transformer is treated as efficient generative-model architecture and inference work under the supplied workshop criterion.
objective_assessments.reason: HLA is centrally an efficient attention architecture for video generation, with supported linear sequence-length complexity and substantial modeled FLOP reductions, directly matching a core EDGE efficiency topic.

assumptions: Narrative results are treated as valid bounded evidence even though exact table-cell values are unavailable in the normalized source.
objective_assessments.reason: The paper supplies a bounded video-diffusion evaluation with named VBench and FLOP metrics, Wan2.1 baselines, resolutions, and variant ablations, but excludes stronger recent attention baselines and the normalized source omits table-cell values.

assumptions: FLOP counts are treated as a computational-efficiency metric rather than a physical latency or energy measurement.
objective_assessments.reason: Supported results compare against Wan2.1 or quadratic attention, quantify FLOP reductions, and expose a slight VBench quality loss, but exact per-variant values and inference timing conditions are unavailable.

assumptions: Training on H100 GPUs does not establish deployment realism for generation-time efficiency.
The mobile-accelerator statement is treated as motivation rather than deployment evidence.
objective_assessments.reason: The relevant efficiency evidence consists chiefly of modeled FLOPs and software-level quality evaluation; the only specified H100 hardware concerns training, while inference hardware and mobile execution are not measured.

assumptions: The omitted comparator families are practically implementable for a controlled benchmark.
Representative mobile or less-capable accelerators can be accessed for device measurements.
objective_assessments.reason: A concrete next experiment can test HLA against the omitted modern linear-attention baselines and measure latency, memory, and energy on less-capable or mobile accelerators.

verdicts.reason: The quoted abstract passage states that conventional linear attention applies kernels independently before pairwise similarities and thereby forms a low-degree rational approximation to softmax.
The quoted passage directly contrasts HLA with prior linear attention by placing the nonlinearity after pairwise similarities.
The source explicitly derives an efficient scheme similar to standard linear attention and states that it avoids time-consuming tensor reshaping.
The complexity section states linear dependence on sequence length and polynomial growth with the number of Hadamard factors.
The data section specifies a 350K OpenSoraPlan subset and about 100K synthetic Wan2.1 14B videos for fine-tuning.
The training-details passage states a 1e-4 learning rate for all models and stages and use of eight H100 GPUs.
The evaluation section explicitly says that windowing, delta-rule, and softmax-linear hybrid variants are not compared.

The main-results section identifies HLA-3F-R1-10, evaluates it with VBench against comparable-parameter models, calls it slightly inferior, and reports about 23% lower computational complexity than Wan2.1-1.3B.
The ablation passage directly reports that more HLA layers slightly reduce VBench scores while reducing computational complexity.
The complexity section directly reports a 20% to 90% FLOP reduction relative to quadratic attention depending on resolution and variant.
The source explicitly frames greater benefit on less-capable, mobile-class accelerators as an expectation, and the claim preserves that non-measured status.
